claims.text: Adding a minor concentration of a refractory microalloying element with suitable processing will induce in situ formation of thermally stable nanoprecipitates.
The resulting nanoprecipitates will be fine and distributed both along grain boundaries and within grains.
The nanoprecipitates will remain thermodynamically stable under the stated elevated-temperature conditions.
The nanoprecipitates will impede dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitates will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will enhance high-temperature yield strength.
Impeded dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will enhance creep resistance.
Between approximately 600°C and 900°C, the microalloyed alloy will have higher yield strength than the unmodified alloy.
Between approximately 600°C and 900°C, the microalloyed alloy will have a lower creep rate than the unmodified alloy under representative mechanical loads.
The predicted benefits may not persist at significantly lower temperatures or where other degradation mechanisms dominate.
The magnitude of the mechanical improvement and the stability of the precipitates may vary with alloy composition and processing parameters.
